messages:
mike-choi: starting prod rollout v2.14.0 -> canary 5% (eu-west-1) :rocket:
deploy-bot: rollout initiated by mike-choi at 2024-11-03T14:12:00Z, canary=5%
sara-nguyen: seeing p95 latency jump on canary hosts, +200ms vs baseline
sara-nguyen: also ~0.3% 5xxs from inference worker, small but rising :thinking_face:
lee_ops: paging oncall (mike-choi) — potential customer impact if ramps
pagerbot: @mike-choi you are on-call — incident created (INC-2024-432) :rotating_light:
mike-choi: acknow — joining
mike-choi: quick check: is this degrader related to batching? any obvious queues?
sara-nguyen: stack traces show OOM reclamation / kv-cache misses. logs: ```ERROR: kv cache miss for shard-2 -> rebuild path````
taylor-p: tagging product: possible model variant misbind? v2.14.0 bundles quantized runtime changes
mike-choi: can we stop the ramp to 25% and hold at 0? deploy-bot please pause
deploy-bot: pause request received — halting further traffic increase. current canary remains at 5%
lee_ops: recommendation from runtime: flip feature-flag fallback to v2.13 runtime for canary traffic while we investigate
sara-nguyen: agree. executing soft kill-switch on the runtime flag for prod canary only
sara-nguyen: command: ```curl -X POST "https://flags.internal/api/flip" -d '{"flag":"runtime_v2_14_enabled","state":false,"scope":"canary"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"```
deploy-bot: flag flip recorded; routing for canary now using runtime_v2_13 (takes ~30s to propagate)
mike-choi: draining canary pods with the v2.14 label, 1m graceful, then verify no new 5xxs
lee_ops: started drain: ```kubectl cordon pod/p-canary-7 && kubectl delete pod/p-canary-7 --grace-period=60```
sara-nguyen: after flag flip and drain, p95 back to expected range, 5xxs down to 0.03% — monitoring looks stable :white_check_mark:
taylor-p: product pinged, they reported a handful (<10) of degraded responses during initial ramp, no major customer outages
mike-choi: ok, we'll abort the rest of the rollout. action items: 1) revert automated rollout (deploy-bot), 2) open PR to pin v2.13 for rolling canaries, 3) postmortem if any customers surfaced errors
deploy-bot: automated rollback command queued — please approve with `/deploy approve rollback v2.14.0`
mike-choi: /deploy approve rollback v2.14.0 — approved
deploy-bot: rollback started; replacing canary pods with v2.13 image, expected completion ~5m
sara-nguyen: post-rollback verification: running smoke prompts against canary endpoints, embedding sanity checks all passing
lee_ops: creating incident summary and adding customers list for outreach: will coordinate with support to notify any affected customers
taylor-p: note for postmortem: investigate quantization interactions with kv-cache and OOM thresholds under burst traffic, add synthetic test that runs at 1.5x token-rate
mike-choi: good. once rollback finishes, we'll leave the feature-flag off and schedule a gated re-roll with extended canary and extra telemetry
pagerbot: INC-2024-432 updated: severity downgraded to P2, status = mitigated
lee_ops: thanks everyone — if anything regresses, re-open here. closing thread in 1h unless we hear otherwise :pray:
